videos.script: Until now, a goroutine waited on one channel at a time. This lesson lets it wait on several. {{select}} Select looks like a switch, and each case is a send or a receive. You ask two sources the same question. The mirror answers in eighty milliseconds, and select takes it. When both cases are ready, select picks one at random. Ten thousand tries split almost exactly in half. {{timeout}} A timeout is just one more case: a channel that delivers when time is up. Where you create it matters. Inside the loop, each step gets a fresh limit. Before the loop, the whole job shares one. {{default}} Then default, which runs when nothing else can. It turns a send into a try. In a loop it turns into a spinning processor: three hundred million polls in one second. {{nil}} Last, a nil channel. Its case can never be chosen, so setting a channel to nil switches its case off. {{close}} Lesson 6 is about the goroutines all of this can leave behind.
